page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor, utilizing the ARM64 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this server features 128.0 GB of system memory, translating to 2.0 GB per core. It is equipped with 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8gd.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core testing, software compilation with Clang, and multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with both cached small-block and uncached large-block read operations ranking in the top tier. Database performance is also notable, with Redis SET operations reaching 133.11 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring in the top tier. Single-core performance, however, remains in the average tier across stress-ng and Geekbench tests.

From a resource density perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications, but provides high compute density per unit of memory. The inclusion of 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage offers high-speed local data access without the overhead of network-attached storage, enhancing qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-heavy workloads. The ARM64 architecture lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX or AMX, which represents a compatibility tradeoff for legacy software, though it compensates with strong native cryptographic acceleration and high-efficiency physics processing.

This server is designed for multi-threaded compute workloads, high-throughput database operations, static web serving, and software compilation. It is also capable of handling medium-scale LLM inference, as evidenced by top-tier text generation speeds with 7B models.
